convoLines.text: "What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Liam. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
«Hei... wote Twi? Daabi? ...hai.»
They answer at length. They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer. "No?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They answer at length. They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
They answer at length. You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. Sounds, and the shape of meaning just out of reach.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said fun was just being around your people. Do we count? Are we trying?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Liam. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
Found something. Follow it to the moot.
Said. At the moot. Let the fire decide what it means.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
«Hallo! Du... wie heißt du?» "Food?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They answer at length. They nod back, a little quicker this time.
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
They answer at length. You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Yeah? What's up?"
Xavier laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — Stimmt.." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
Emmett has an edge today — something curdled.

"It's my sister, Zita. Was taken at the Scattering. The boring half, they said — my sister, boring. I think about that every day. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming.
Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"They took Fatima and Rafael — The Auction, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Emmett grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Emmett is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here? Funny how that works."
"Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset."
"Being a taxi driver taught me to read people fast — who's lying, who's scared, who needs a job. Turns out that's a survival skill. Who knew. No time to waste."
"Still on your useful old-life skills."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "The Auction. They just... took Fatima and Rafael. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Emmett nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Ask me tomorrow. Everything changes by tomorrow."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said patience was your old-life superpower — really waiting, without fidgeting. Still your answer?"
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff. But what do I know."
They let that thread drop — for now.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Pit. They just... took Fatima. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I show up. That's my part."

deathBeat: d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Piper Qiu is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d10: 🕯️ Piper Qiu is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d10: The village's quarrel was with Piper — and Piper is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d11: That night, they bring Piper home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d10: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d10: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."

d10: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.
d11: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 51. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."

lines: d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Piper Qiu is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d10: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d10: 🕯️ Piper Qiu is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d10: What Piper kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d10: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Raj blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d10: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d10: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d10: 📖 LEARNED: Debris Shelter (Level 1). A lean-to of branches and leaves beats nothing. Dead air is insulation.
d10: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d10: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d10: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Piper Qiu, 10 days. The mantle passes to Raj Casey.
d10: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Raj Casey, 53 — a glazier. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm.
d10: The village's quarrel was with Piper — and Piper is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d10: The fire knew Raj before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
